newsitem.title: ITALY: France says delighted UN finally moving on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France says delighted UN finally moving on Zaire.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Friday he was delighted that the United Nations was acting on the Zaire crisis and welcomed an agreement in principle by the United States to join a planned relief force.
"I am delighted to see that things are finally moving," he said in a speech to the U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit.

The Security Council was expected on Friday to authorise the deployment of a Canadian-led multinational force to bring food, water and medicines to more than a million Rwandan Hutu refugees stranded by fighting in eastern Zaire.
Hundreds of thousands of them began heading home on Friday in a trek that could signal a breakthrough in humanitarian attempts to keep them from starving.
Diplomats said the force was expected to include troops from Canada, the United States, France, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands, South Africa and Senegal.
"We welcome the decision in principle of the United States in favour of the deployment of this multinational force and we hope that it will be able to be set up as soon as possible," Juppe said.
France has been one of the sharpest critics of the world's slowness to respond to the tragedy in eastern Zaire.

"I note, in passing, very often, often wrongly, the slowness and passivity of the United Nations. But the U.N., we know, only gains its capacity for initiative from the will and diligence of its member states," Juppe said.
